title: Calling `fetch` with a `Request` and `next: { revalidate : <any value> }` produces spurious warning

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/dkokotov/nextjs-cache-revalidate-spurious-warning

### To Reproduce

Run the reproduction app (either development or production).
View the console output - there is a warning 

```
 ⚠ fetch for https://example.com/page on / specified "cache: default" and "revalidate: 1000", only one should be specified.
```

which should not be there

### Current vs. Expected behavior

The result of 

```
  await fetch(new Request('https://example.com/page'), {
    next: {
      revalidate: 1000
    }
  });

```

produces warning `fetch for https://example.com/page on / specified "cache: default" and "revalidate: 1000", only one should be specified.`, even though we did not specify a value for `cache`.

### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 23.0.0: Fri Sep 15 14:41:43 PDT 2023; root:xnu-10002.1.13~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000
Binaries:
  Node: 20.8.0
  npm: 10.1.0
  Yarn: 1.22.19
  pnpm: 8.7.5
Relevant Packages:
  next: 14.0.2-canary.15
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 18.2.0
  react-dom: 18.2.0
  typescript: 5.1.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```


### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

App Router, Data fetching (gS(S)P, getInitialProps)

### Additional context

The behavior  happens both on dev and production. It's mostly harmless, but annoying to see extra warnings.

Note that calling

```
  await fetch('https://example.com/page2', {
    next: {
      revalidate: 1000
    }
  });

```

does not produce the warning.

This happens I think because when passing a `Request` as first param to `fetch`, all the fields have values, and so the check in the code (https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/server/lib/patch-fetch.ts#L265) produces a false positive). It should be changed to only test the case where first param is a url.
